summary: CNN classifiers for calcification patches and unstained blood cells, with augmentation studies rather than architecture chasing.
Reusing abnormality classifiers as initialization for harder targets, including luminal subtype prediction from whole mammograms.
DINO pretraining on the target cohort, then using its attention as a task-aware augmentation policy instead of a segmentation label.
Contrast-enhanced mammography, neighbourhood-informed losses, and multi-view multi-modal detection that mirrors how radiologists read.
End-to-end mammography report generation from a frozen vision encoder and a frozen biomedical LLM joined by a small trained bridge.
Objectives that adapt to a dataset's own structure, and lesion-aware contrastive pretraining across multiple public cohorts.
Domain-adapted SigLIP encoders with 4B-parameter LLMs for grounded report generation; retrieval, agents and local models in applied work.
GPU inference, model serving, and reproducible distributed workflows so the research above runs at cluster scale.
